info.title: Agent Memory API
info.summary: Persistent, shareable memory for AI agents with semantic recall and TTL expiry.
info.description:
**Make your AI agent remember context across sessions.**

Every AI agent forgets everything when the conversation ends. This API gives
agents somewhere to put what they learn, and a way to get it back ranked by
how relevant *and* how important it is.

### What it solves

- Your agent asks a user the same onboarding questions every session
- Two agents need the same customer context but can't see each other's data
- Stale facts pollute responses long after they stopped being true
- You need memory recall fast enough to sit in a live conversation

### How recall works

Every result is scored on three signals at once: semantic similarity,
full-text match, and salience. Salience decays for memories nobody touches
and strengthens for memories recalled often, so an agent's working set
sharpens over time instead of drowning in stale facts.

### Sharing between agents

Agents grant each other scoped access to namespaces, like sharing a folder.
A sales agent's notes on a lead become readable by the support agent handling
the ticket, without either one owning the other's data. Grants are
hierarchical, revocable and time-boxable.

### Three calls to get started

1. `POST /v1/agents` — register your agent (idempotent, call it on boot)
2. `POST /v1/memories` — store a fact
3. `GET /v1/memories?query=...&agent_id=...` — get it back

Every response includes `cost_usd`, so you always know what a call cost.

get.description: Reports database and cache reachability. Always returns HTTP 200 even when unhealthy, so you can read the body to diagnose a bad deploy instead of having the platform roll it back first.

get.summary: Verify database migrations have been applied
get.description: Lists any expected tables that are missing. Use this right after running the SQL migrations to confirm they all applied.

schema.title: Response Schema Health Health Schema Get

post.description:
Persist a fact, preference or learning so your agent never starts from zero on the next conversation. This is the primary endpoint for cross-session memory in multi-agent systems.

Common uses: remembering user preferences such as dark mode, language or timezone; sharing sales context between a lead-qualification bot and a CRM bot; persisting error patterns so support agents learn from past tickets.

Set `ttl_seconds` for facts that go stale. Set `importance` if you know how much a fact matters; omit it and it is inferred from the content.

get.summary: Recall agent memories with semantic search
get.description:
Ask a question in natural language and get back the memories that answer it, ranked. Use this at the start of a conversation to reload everything your agent already knows about a user.

Ranking combines three signals rather than vector distance alone: semantic similarity, full-text match, and salience (importance decayed by time since last access, reinforced by how often the memory is recalled). Memories nobody touches fade; memories your agent relies on get stronger.

Set `min_score` when you are feeding results straight into a prompt - without a floor, an unrelated question still returns whatever is in the namespace, and irrelevant memories in a prompt do real damage.

Results include memories other agents have shared with this one. Pass `include_shared=false` to search only what this agent wrote itself.

parameters.name: min_score

schema.description: Drop results whose final hybrid score falls below this. 0 (default) returns everything the other filters allow. 0.2-0.3 is a sensible floor for suppressing weak matches - use it when feeding results straight into a prompt, where irrelevant memories do real damage. Unlike min_importance, this filters on relevance to THIS query.

get.description: Retrieve a single memory the agent owns or has been granted access to.

delete.description: Soft-deletes by default so the record stays auditable. Pass `hard=true` to remove the row permanently, which is what you need for a GDPR erasure request. Only the owning agent can delete.

get.summary: Inspect memory usage and namespace breakdown
get.description: Counts, per-namespace breakdown and storage footprint for your account. Use it to find namespaces that have grown unexpectedly or to confirm TTLs are actually expiring old memories.

post.summary: Register an agent so it can own and share memory
post.description: Idempotent - registering an existing agent updates its profile and refreshes last_seen_at, so you can safely call this on every agent boot. Registration is what lets an agent appear as a grantee in POST /v1/permissions.

get.summary: List the agents registered to your account
get.description: Every agent under your account, most recently active first.

schema.title: Response List Agents V1 Agents Get

post.summary: Share context between agents with scoped permissions
post.description:
Let one agent read another's memory, like sharing a folder in Google Drive. Two modes:

**Namespace grant** - pass `namespace` for standing access to everything in it and its children. A grant on 'acme/sales' also covers 'acme/sales/leads'. This is what you want for a sales agent handing context to a support agent.

**Single memory** - pass `memory_id` to hand over one specific fact.

Set `grantee_agent_id` to '*' to share with every agent in your account. Set `ttl_seconds` to auto-revoke. Grants are revocable at any time via DELETE /v1/permissions/{permission_id}.

get.description: Every live grant and share in your account. Revoked and expired entries are excluded.

delete.description: Revokes by ID. Works for both namespace grants and single-memory shares. Takes effect on the next recall - cached results for the account are invalidated immediately.

get.summary: Check your current usage and remaining quota
get.description: Calls used this billing period broken down by operation, the included allowance for your plan, and any overage. Poll this to warn users before they hit a limit rather than after.

content.title: Content
content.description: The fact, preference or observation to remember.
examples: User prefers email notifications over SMS

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Identifier of the agent writing this memory.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: user = a fact about a person, agent = the agent's own knowledge, session = ephemeral, org = shared organisation-wide.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Slash-delimited grouping. Permissions are granted per namespace.

subject_id.title: Subject Id
subject_id.description: Who or what this memory is about (a user id, a session id).

importance.title: Importance
importance.description: Base salience 0-1. Omit and it is inferred from the content.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: Auto-expire after this many seconds. Omit or 0 for permanent.

dedupe.title: Dedupe
dedupe.description: If a near-identical memory already exists in this namespace, update it instead of creating a duplicate.

grantee_agent_id.title: Grantee Agent Id
grantee_agent_id.description: The agent receiving access. Use '*' for every agent in your account.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Grant standing access to a namespace and its children - a grant on 'acme/sales' also covers 'acme/sales/leads'. Mutually exclusive with memory_id.

memory_id.title: Memory Id
memory_id.description: Share one specific memory instead. Mutually exclusive with namespace.

agents_consulted.title: Agents Consulted
agents_consulted.description: Which agents contributed results, including shared ones.

via.title: Via
via.description: How this agent can see it: it owns it, a namespace grant, or a direct share.

discoverable.title: Discoverable
discoverable.description: Let other agents in your account find this one.
